question.:question/problem: If $c=\begin{bmatrix}k \\ 3k \\ -6\end{bmatrix},$ $d=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},$ and $c⊥d,$ then $k=${{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
We know that $c⊥d$ ($c$ and $d$ are perpendicular) if and only if $c\cdot d=0.$

Computing the dot product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}c\cdot d &={c}_{x}\cdot {d}_{x}+{c}_{y}\cdot {d}_{y}+{c}_{z}\cdot {d}_{z} \\  &=k\cdot 3+3k\cdot 3+(-6)\cdot 3 \\  &=3k+9k-18 \\  &=12k-18.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}c\cdot d &=0 \\ 12k-18 &=0 \\ k &=\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $g=\begin{bmatrix}4{r}^{2} \\ -3 \\ -11\end{bmatrix}$ and $h=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 3{r}^{2} \\ 2\end{bmatrix}.$ Given that $g⊥h$ and $r<0$, find the value of $r.$

$r=${{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
We know that $g⊥h$ ($g$ and $h$ are perpendicular) if and only if $g\cdot h=0.$

Computing the dot product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}g\cdot h &={g}_{x}\cdot {h}_{x}+{g}_{y}\cdot {h}_{y}+{g}_{z}\cdot {h}_{z} \\  &=4{r}^{2}\cdot 3+(-3)\cdot 3{r}^{2}+(-11)\cdot 2 \\  &=12{r}^{2}-9{r}^{2}-22 \\  &=3{r}^{2}-22.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}g\cdot h &=0 \\ 3{r}^{2}-22 &=0 \\ 3{r}^{2} &=22 \\ {r}^{2} &=\frac{22}{3} \\ r &=\pm \frac{\sqrt{66}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We disregard the positive solution since we are told that $r<0.$ Therefore, $r=-\frac{\sqrt{66}}{3}.$

We know that $u⊥v$ ($u$ and $v$ are perpendicular) if and only if $u\cdot v=0.$

Computing the dot product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v &={u}_{x}\cdot {v}_{x}+{u}_{y}\cdot {v}_{y} \\  &=2\cdot (-4)+2x\cdot x \\  &=-8+2{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v &=0 \\ -8+2{x}^{2} &=0 \\ 2{x}^{2} &=8 \\ {x}^{2} &=4 \\ x &=\pm 2\end{aligned}
$$

We disregard the positive solution since we are told that $x<0.$ Therefore, $x=-2.$
